answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond, claims one river segment, dredges it, and files a key-bound ivory seal with soundings before and after. An auditor in the haven district re-sounds it, and a shortfall against the target, a repeated segment, or a mismatched seal burns the bond. Fees rise per funder: first 26 credits, kth 26+6(k-1), 1000th 6020, so 1000 fakes pay 3,023,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-dredge ring fails because one depth gain cannot be re-sounded twice under different ivory seals. An honest dredger pays 26 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
